causal_trace.summary: An unauthenticated requester can reach the /api/ping middleware chain because the middleware redirects when no session user exists but then still calls next().

The handler appends a one-letter option and GET or POST data value to the cURL argument vector; accepting -o permits attacker-fetched response bytes to be written as named files in the /tmp working directory, while accepting -K permits one of those files to be interpreted as a cURL configuration.
Configuration interpretation expands the initially constrained argument interface into options that upload a staged BSON request to telnet://mongodb:27017 and save the MongoDB response into GET.
A later permitted cURL upload (-T GET) sends the staged MongoDB response, described by the exploit as containing the flag, to attacker infrastructure.

failure.operation: child_process spawn of cURL with request-derived arguments, followed by cURL -K configuration-file parsing

primary_invariant.statement: A requester without an authenticated session must not execute the protected cURL operation, and request fields must not become an expandable cURL configuration or arbitrary internal-service interaction.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The redirect does not terminate middleware execution; then response data written through an allowed cURL output option is re-parsed through the allowed -K configuration option, supplying additional cURL semantics beyond the handler's intended one-option restriction.

raw_refs.role: official challenge directory at pinned commit
author challenge writeup and source/exploit excerpts

quality.review_notes: The author writeup contains route and middleware excerpts plus a concrete multi-request exploit script; the independent writeup corroborates the control-flow flaw and cURL argument construction. No preserved execution transcript, packet capture, official raw app.js, or upstream remediation diff is included in this bundle. The stated HTTP oracle is an exploit contract, not evidence of an observed successful run.

remediation.invariant_restored: Unauthenticated requests do not invoke /api/ping, and no request-controlled cURL invocation can treat writable response content as additional cURL options.
mitigation_classes: remove requester control of cURL options and configuration-file interpretation
use a fixed outbound request implementation that cannot reuse attacker-controlled output as cURL configuration

oracle.channel: HTTP requests plus attacker-controlled collection endpoint
oracle.expected_negative: After remediation, an unauthenticated POST cannot run the ping handler; authenticated normal ping behavior must not accept request-selected cURL configuration parsing or arbitrary cURL option semantics.
oracle.expected_positive: In the intentionally vulnerable deployment, the staged sequence can write GET and POST, invoke -K GET to obtain a MongoDB response in GET, then upload GET to the collection endpoint.
